```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A has documented, sourced evidence of payers spending real money on this problem. Cole County, MO paid $7,000 for a compliance tool in March 2026. CivicPlus/AudioEye quoted the Town of Templeton $2,510. Idea B shows no observed purchase by a target buyer, only competitor list prices.",
    "A's urgency is external and dated: the DOJ rule sets April 2027 and April 2028 deadlines, sourced to ADA.gov and the Federal Register. Buyers have a reason to act within a window. B's pain is chronic and self-described, with no forcing event.",
    "A's demand quotes come from named officials describing a specific operational burden ('None of my people are IT people'). B's quotes describe indecision in general and do not point to buying a tool.",
    "B's unit economics look weak on its own evidence. A ~$104 cost per lead set against a $60 one-off price, plus a niche of five near-identical competitors, leaves little room for a solo entrant to find a first customer cheaply.",
    "A's low-end entry point is buildable and priced. GovAccess sells a $149/month scanner on commodity scanning and remediation tech, so a scanner plus prioritized fix list is a plausible six-week MVP with a known price anchor.",
    "A has serious risks of its own. Municipal procurement and insurance burdens, liability for compliance claims, entrenched incumbents, and possible further deadline slippage all threaten a 90-day close. The brief offers no evidence on how long procurement takes."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's LinkedIn demand quote, 'Once you've got 2 real options, the spreadsheet can't choose between them. Only you can.', argues that the final decision cannot be outsourced to a tool. It undercuts B's value proposition rather than supporting willingness to pay. The vendor admission that a human must verify every number and recommendation compounds the problem.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A wins on the strength of its evidence: actual municipal spend, a dated regulatory deadline, and named-official pain. Its main unaddressed risk is reaching a paying customer within 90 days. Neither brief provides procurement-timeline or conversion data, and A's solo-vendor liability and insurance questions are open. If municipal buying proves slower than 90 days, B's faster self-serve purchase path could matter more, but B currently shows no evidence of demand converting to payment."
}
```
